entries.title: Stop more inputs from being run as commands

ai.title: Expand terminal command skip list and add word count limit
ai.summary: Added help, find, and kill to SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS in common/src/constants.ts. Updated npm-app/src/cli.ts to reject user inputs with 4 or more words before execution. This prevents benign text or complex sentences from triggering terminal commands.

eli5.text: Today the terminal refuses to run any short message that is four words long or longer. If you type a phrase such as 'show me the way' the assistant won’t try to run it as a command; it will ask you again. At the same time, words like help, find, and kill are now blocked even when they start your message, so benign prompts or accidental system words can no longer trigger a shell command.

ai.title: Add bump-version script and litestar start command
ai.summary: Replaced `scripts/build-version-info.js` with `scripts/bump-version.ts` to increment patch versions in `npm-app/package.json` and `backend/package.json`, exposed via new `bump` script in root `package.json`. Added `start-litestar` command to `npm-app/package.json` and root `package.json` for testing against a mock Litestar project. Updated `todo.knowledge.md` to mark two tasks as complete and add a new note regarding file overwriting.

eli5.text: The version of the software was bumped from 1.0.57 to 1.0.58, and a new command was added that lets developers start the assistant pointed at a test project built with the Litestar framework. This live today: after updating, anyone running the new start command will see the assistant initialize against Litestar sample files instead of the default project, and both the main package and the backend package now report the same newer version number.

ai.title: Skip lib checks in common tsconfig
ai.summary: Added skipLibCheck: true to common/tsconfig.json to bypass type-checking of external declaration files. Pinned typescript to 5.5.4 in npm-app/package.json, removing caret range. Affects shared core compilation and npm-app dependency resolution. Reduces build time and prevents errors from upstream type definition mismatches.

eli5.text: The software no longer double-checks the fine print of outside tool packages before building, so your projects start up a bit faster and won't trip over mismatched paperwork from shared packages. It affects the shared core compilation and the npm-app dependency resolution. The team also pinned a key build tool to an exact version instead of a range, making builds more predictable. This is live today.
